name: Shuni
overview: Shuni was a male member of the tribe of Gad, known specifically as a son of Gad. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational genealogy of the Israelite people. His descendants are associated with the Shunites, a clan within the tribe of Gad.
namesAndTitles: The name Shuni appears as a proper name in the Scriptures without an explicit meaning provided. There are no special titles or divine naming attributed to Shuni in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shuni as a son of Gad, establishing his place within the tribe of Gad. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shuni's significance lies in his role as one of the sons of Gad who journeyed to Egypt with the family of Israel, a crucial event in the unfolding story of God's covenant people. His mention helps trace the lineage and tribal divisions that shaped Israel's identity. The reference to the Shunites in later texts connects his descendants to the broader tribal structure of Israel, emphasizing continuity in God's providential plan.
